card: Ensures bitcoin-cli respects -rpcclienttimeout while transmitting RPC requests. Currently, if an RPC server holds a socket open without reading data, socket wait timeouts cause bitcoin-cli to loop and wait indefinitely instead of aborting. The PR updates HTTPClient::SendRequest to return failure on Sock::Wait timeouts or socket errors, fixing a regression introduced during the removal of libevent in #36299.
evidence: Commit e5d9a7e04b: 'Before 1805716354, the `continue` was the route to the deadline check. That commit removed the deadline, so a Sock::Wait() timeout silently started waiting again, forever. This means -rpcclienttimeout is never respected when sending: bitcoin-cli will hang for as long as the server keeps the connection open without reading the request.'
problem: When an RPC server accepts a connection but does not read from the socket, bitcoin-cli hangs indefinitely. A previous refactor (#36299) removed the overall deadline check while continuing to loop on Sock::Wait() timeouts, causing -rpcclienttimeout to be ignored during request sending.

risk.why: A mistake would only affect the bitcoin-cli client tool and could cause RPC requests to abort prematurely on slow connections.

scope_notes: A tiny single-file fix (+2/-1) in the RPC client socket handling code.
summary: Fixes a bug in bitcoin-cli where HTTPClient::SendRequest loops indefinitely if the socket does not become writable. It changes socket wait timeouts and errors during request transmission to immediately return a failure instead of retrying forever, ensuring -rpcclienttimeout is respected.
